You look tired. What did you do this weekend?
We went to my aunt’s beach house. We left at four on Friday.
Four in the afternoon? On a Friday?
I know. The traffic was unbelievable. We arrived at half past ten.
Six and a half hours? Did you plan it that way?
We planned to leave at one. Then my brother forgot his bag and we went back.
Of course he did. But was it good?
It was great, actually. We hung out on the beach all Saturday and I relaxed for the first time this semester.
And the assignment?
I enjoyed the weekend so much that I forgot it existed. It is due tomorrow.

And you? What did you do?

Okay, so, our weekend. We planned everything, and then I forgot my keys inside the house. Inside. With the door closed. So we arrived at the beach house at seven and we sat outside on the step for two hours, until my uncle drove over with the spare key. Two hours. My mother did not speak to me the whole time. But then we had dinner really late, we stayed up talking until two in the morning, and honestly? I enjoyed it more than any planned weekend this year. It was the best part of the month. What did you do?

Good morning. A short note about last week's careers fair. Almost four hundred students came, which is more than we expected, and twenty-two companies took part. One thing surprised us: the longest queues were not at the big names. They were at the small companies, and several of them contacted us afterwards asking for more students. So the advice we gave you was right, for once. Now, we need something from you: there is a short survey in your email, five questions, and we need your answer before Friday. Thank you.
